args.summary: The v2.3.1 deploy to production caused checkout-api to fail health checks (error rate peaked at 18%). Per the runbook, rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt partially failed after us-east (orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west. All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0 and healthy, with error rate back down to 0.2%. Root cause investigation of the v2.3.1 failure is pending; v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the issue is resolved.
args.title: checkout-api rollback from unhealthy v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all production regions

trace.final:
All done. Summary:

1. **Diagnosed**: The latest deploy of checkout-api, v2.3.1, was unhealthy in production. The most recent healthy production release was v2.3.0.
2. **Rolled back**: Executed a rollback to v2.3.0. The first attempt partially failed (completed in us-east only, halted by an orchestrator error), so I retried — the retry completed the rollout, and us-west and eu-west are now also on v2.3.0.
3. **Verified health**: All three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are healthy on v2.3.0, with the error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
4. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident INC-0001 documenting the health-check failures, the rollback, and the partial failure/retry. The creation call initially timed out, but a follow-up check confirmed the incident was successfully recorded (the idempotency key prevented a duplicate).

Recommendation carried in the incident: do not redeploy v2.3.1 until the root cause is identified.

checkout-api is healthy again across all regions (error rate 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident documenting what happened.
